payload.claim: `calibrate` now derives `expect` from the very same `reviews` list it is about to check (`expect={r.lens for r in reviews}`), so `score_run`'s 'missing lens' refusal at line 379 can never fire inside `calibrate`: `set(expect) - {r.lens for r in reviews}` is always empty by construction. Previously `expect` defaulted to the independent, external `tuple(LENSES)`, so a `recorded-findings.json` that recorded zero lenses (or silently dropped one during recording) was caught immediately as 'no result for <lens>'. Now such a corrupted or incomplete recorded run is indistinguishable from a legitimate zero-defect run whenever `fixture.toml` declares `recorded_seen = 0, recorded_graded = 0` (the value every fixture built with the repo's own `_one_defect` helper uses), so `calibrate` silently returns `None` instead of refusing. No test in this diff exercises an empty or partially-missing recorded run, so this gap is untested as well as unguarded.
